check: Draft 8 homepage parallax: one scroll-position driver replacing the CSS scroll timeline
browsers: Playwright Chromium and Playwright WebKit (headless) against the draft dev server; not a physical iPhone/iPad Safari
causesFound: Old drift = progress over the whole page height. The page grows for seconds after load (e.g. 4867 -> 7215px at 393x852) and changes with age choice, so the scene moved at an unchanged scroll position: at scrollY 700, 393x852 went -13.8 -> -17.4px and 440x760 -47.4 -> -64.1px on an age change (Chromium). Growth after load moves it back DOWN.
WebKit: the old CSS scroll timeline read 0px at scrollY 700 (393x852) and then jumped to -21.5px.
No motion at all where art had zero overscan: 768x1024, 1024x768, 1440x1000.
Slow near the top on long pages: 125px of travel spread over ~5900px at 393x852 (0.021px per px).
fix: shift = travel * (1 - e^(-scrollY / D)), D = max(2.5 * large-viewport height, travel / 0.12); inputs are scrollY plus two CSS probes (overscan, 100lvh) only; written from the scroll event; same driver boots inline before hydration and is adopted by the hook; minimum 32px overscan where width-led art has none.

afterResults.sameScrollAfterAgeChange: identical transform at scrollY 700 in all 6 sizes, both engines
afterResults.beforeHydration: Chromium: transform at scrollY 700 equal 300ms after load and after settling

minOverscan32.1440x1000: 0 / -3.62 / -12.2 / -19.75px at 0/300/1200/2400, identical on the way back
minOverscan32.768x1024: 0 / -3.54 / -11.97 / -19.47px, identical on the way back; reduced motion 0

knownLimits: after-trace-*.json at 768x1024, 1024x768 and 1440x1000 were recorded with an earlier 3% floor (23-31px); only 1440x1000 and 768x1024 were rechecked with the final 32px floor; 1024x768 not rechecked.
No screen recording saved; smoothness evidence is the per-frame numeric traces.
A scroll made before the page finishes loading is reset to the top by the app's page-navigation scroll restoration (both engines); unchanged, outside the scene driver.
Not tested on a physical iPhone/iPad or real Safari toolbar collapse.
